source: Internet Archive djen-tjro-2025 OCR cadernos (public DJEN publications) for the original 20-doc seed; TJRO JURIS system (src/tjro_juris, real digitally-native court text, not OCR) for the 20-doc expansion batch, the 20-doc preliminar-targeted Round A batch, the 20-doc costs/fees-targeted Round B batch, the 18-doc general-volume Round C batch, the 8-doc honorarios_fim-targeted Round D batch, the 25-doc model-assisted-correction Round E batch (2017-07-ACORDAO.parquet), and the 20-doc Round F batch (2023-09-SENTENCA.parquet, via Internet Archive item tjro-juris-2023) -- Round F's text is Gemini-sourced but its final labels are model-assisted-corrected, see notes
per_class_note: Counts above are train-split only, matching the original convention. Round D closed the last G2 gap: honorarios_fim went from 6 to 12 in train (>=10 minimum). Round E (25 docs, see notes) added structural-category volume across the board (e.g. acordao_decisorio_fim 21->37, cabecalho_inicio 69->92, voto_inicio 22->40) by deliberately excluding ref_normativa from its own labeling effort -- ref_normativa was already the single most abundant category (824 examples pre-Round-E, already far past any minimum) so Round E's per-document labeling budget was spent entirely on the structural anchors an audited-precision pass on this same checkpoint had just shown to be the model's weakest categories (resultado/cabecalho/voto/relatorio/acordao_decisorio pairs). Round E's ref_normativa count (931) comes only from spans the correcting subagents happened to keep/fix from the model's own predictions, not from fresh labeling. Round F (20 sentenca docs, see notes) closed the G5 volume gate (131->151 total docs, >=150 minimum): it lifted fundamentacao_legal, dispositivo_abertura, and the custas/honorarios/preliminar pairs the most, since sentencas structurally carry these far more densely than the acordao-heavy prior rounds. The counts above already reflect Round F's POST-CORRECTION labels (see verification_note) -- the raw Gemini output before correction had materially different, worse per-class numbers (e.g. several dispositivo_abertura/resultado spans were simply wrong or missing) and was never merged into these totals as-is. ALL G1, G2, and G5 gates are now clear across every split; only G4 (waived, multi-tribunal) remains.
labeler: prompt_subagents:haiku (original 20-doc seed, one labeling subagent per batch, acordaos first); prompt_subagents:general-purpose, one per document, for the 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch, the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch, the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch, the 8-doc Round D honorarios_fim-targeted batch, the 25-doc Round E model-assisted-correction batch, and the 20-doc Round F model-assisted-correction batch (draft from llm_annotator:gemini-2.5-flash + gemini-2.5-flash-lite via litellm, corrected by prompt_subagents:general-purpose, one per document, using a 20-subagent audit pass as the correction brief)
verification_note: IMPORTANT provenance distinction: the original 20-doc seed's val+test went through a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble verification pass before being trusted as eval-quality gold. The 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch (tjro_juris_acordao_prelim_*), the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_costs_*), the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_vol_*), the 8-doc Round D batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_hon_*), the 25-doc Round E model-assisted-correction batch, and the 20-doc Round F batch have NOT gone through that ensemble verification -- each has single-subagent labeling (one general-purpose agent per document, each independently briefed with the full annotation guideline), mechanical validation (opf_annotate.py validate: 0 offset/overlap/label-space errors across all splits), and a manual spot-check of a sample of records by the orchestrating session (not exhaustive, not the full ensemble). Round E additionally started from a trained checkpoint's own predictions plus an independent 25-subagent audit of those predictions (correct/wrong_category/wrong_boundary/false_positive verdicts, computed for a separate precision study before the correction pass began) rather than a blank annotation guideline read; each correcting subagent was instructed to keep audit-confirmed-correct spans, fix or drop flawed ones, and then do its own fresh full-document read for anything the audit hadn't touched (the audit only judged the model's own predicted spans, not the whole document). Round F's ORIGINAL labeling mode was different from every other batch -- not subagent-labeled at all, but LLM-annotated (Gemini 2.5 Flash / Flash-Lite via litellm, regex-anchored spans resolved locally to character offsets) with no independent review. That raw Gemini output was subsequently audited (20 subagents, one per doc, judging every predicted span correct/wrong_category/wrong_boundary/false_positive against the guideline, plus noting missed anchors) and found materially flawed: only 217/357 predicted spans (61%) were fully correct, with 107 wrong_boundary (dominant bug: ref_normativa/fundamentacao_legal citations systematically dropping the leading "art."/"artigo"/"Resolução" token), 17 false_positive (including quote-contamination -- spans lifted from a block-quoted precedent inside the reasoning, and hallucinated valor_condenacao on cases with no actual condemnation), and 16 wrong_category, plus 124 noted missed anchors (most consequentially: the real dispositivo_abertura/resultado operative phrases were repeatedly missed or mistagged onto the wrong text). A second wave of 20 correction subagents (same pattern as Round E: draft = Gemini prediction + audit verdict, subagent keeps/fixes/drops/adds per the verdict then does its own fresh read for the rest) turned this into the FINAL, corrected 456-span labels now merged into train/val/test -- the raw, uncorrected Gemini output was never merged as-is. Round F is therefore best described as Gemini-drafted, subagent-corrected -- closer in process and confidence to Round E than to a pure-LLM batch, though its draft passed through an extra flawed intermediate stage Round E didn't have. Treat Round F, and every batch from these rounds' val/test docs, as provisional-quality until they receive the same ensemble verification pass the original seed used, especially before reporting any eval metric that includes them.
notes: Seed gold built the subagent way: strict sampling (acordao requires ACORDAO+VOTO+ACORDAM, sentenca requires SENTENCA+dispositivo-formula+operative-verb; despachos excluded), Haiku labeling subagents returning {category,match,nth}, offsets resolved by opf_annotate from-spans, overlaps removed deterministically, then a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble over val+test. ref_normativa was originally excluded (regex pre-pass at inference) but was added back to the trained label space and bootstrapped into every split via the same regex pre-pass (scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py) against the already-verified gold text -- see git history for the architecture decision and the regex fix (thousands-separator article numbers, spelled-out inciso/paragrafo/alinea) that preceded it. A second real bug was found and fixed in scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py's merge_with_opf_spans: it only reliably favored a gold/model span over an overlapping regex span on an exact start-position tie, not on the more common case of a regex match starting earlier but still partially overlapping -- a real gold custas_fim span was being silently dropped by this before the fix. 20-doc JURIS expansion batch added 2026-07-16 (see verification_note above) via the same subagent-labeling + opf_annotate.py from-spans/validate pipeline as the original seed, sourced from src/tjro_juris rather than DJEN cadernos. A follow-up 20-doc Round A batch (also 2026-07-16) closed the preliminar_inicio/fim zero-support gap: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2024-08-ACORDAO.parquet for a literal '\\b1\\.\\s*PRELIMINARES?\\b' numbered-heading match (found via manual audit that this heading convention is real but recent -- zero hits in 2005/2008/2017 samples, 21 hits in 2024-08 alone), then subagent-labeled the same way; all 20 confirmed a genuine preliminar section, split 14/3/3 train/val/test (seed 771). A follow-up 20-doc Round B batch (also 2026-07-16) targeted custas_fim/honorarios_fim/fundamentacao_legal: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2022-02-SENTENCA.parquet for both 'custas' and 'honorarios' substring mentions (excluding the 10 sentenca ids already used in the earlier expansion batch); several subagents independently anchored custas and honorarios on the exact same fused-clause span (a genuine ambiguity in Juizado Especial boilerplate, not an agent error -- the guideline explicitly allowed it), which opf_annotate validate correctly rejected as BIOES overlaps; 13 such conflicts were resolved deterministically by keeping the first-listed span and dropping the duplicate, then the batch was split 14/3/3 with a hand-picked (not random) val/test doc selection to guarantee each weak category met its per-split minimum despite the tiny (5-20 doc) supply for some categories. An 18-doc Round C batch (also 2026-07-16) pulled a fresh, unfiltered SENTENCA sample from TJRO JURIS's 2020-10-SENTENCA.parquet (a file not used by any prior batch) purely for G5 volume, split 12/3/3 (random, seed 773) -- it produced zero new honorarios_fim, a real finding about how rare that specific closing shape is, not a labeling gap; that finding directly informed Round D's pre-filter design (also 2026-07-16), which specifically excluded the fused 'custas e/ou honorarios' phrasing and targeted homologacao-de-acordo sentencas instead, yielding 7/8 clean honorarios_fim hits and closing the last G2 gap (see per_class_note). A 25-doc Round E batch (2026-07-16) took a different shape from A-D: 25 genuinely novel documents (2017-07-ACORDAO.parquet, a source year never touched by any prior round -- existing gold was all 2020/2022/2024) were run through the extended 10-epoch checkpoint's own inference, independently audited span-by-span by 25 subagents for a precision study (52.9% audited precision, structural pair categories the weakest), then a second wave of 25 correction subagents turned that prediction+audit pair into full corrected gold per document (keep-confirmed / fix-flawed / drop-false-positive / fresh-read-for-the-rest), all acordaos, split 17/4/4 train/val/test (random, seed 2017). Round E deliberately skipped ref_normativa as new labeling effort (see per_class_note) since it was already the most oversupplied category by a wide margin; this also means Round E's per-doc labeling cost was lower than A-D's from-scratch full reads. While reconciling Round E into this manifest, a pre-existing doc_types_total arithmetic bug was also fixed: it previously read acordao:46/sentenca:80 (sum 126) which didn't match the sum of doc_types_per_split (sum 106, matching the true total) -- corrected to acordao:38/sentenca:68 as the pre-Round-E baseline, then Round E's 25 acordaos were added on top. Single-tribunal (TJRO) corpus of 131 docs; G5 volume (needs >=150 total, currently 131) and the waived G4 multi-tribunal gate remain before this gold clears every readiness gate for a real (non --smoke) training run. A 20-doc Round F batch (2026-07-16), prompted by an explicit request to use Gemini for more data, closed G5: 24 sentenca candidates were strict-sampled (same SENTENCA+dispositivo-cue+operative-verb filter as Round C/D, regex-based) from TJRO JURIS's 2023-09-SENTENCA.parquet -- fetched fresh from the Internet Archive item tjro-juris-2023, a source year never touched by any prior round -- then annotated by Gemini (not subagents) via litellm's regex-anchored batch pipeline (scripts/annotate_with_llm.py's approach, reimplemented locally to avoid pulling in that script's unrelated ibis dependency): the model returns a unique-in-document regex pattern with a capturing group per span, which is resolved locally to exact character offsets rather than trusting model-reported offsets directly. This ran into the Gemini free tier's per-key daily request quota (as low as 20 RPD on one of the three rotating keys in GEMINI_API_KEYS, matching the existing quota-avoidance pattern already established in src/causaganha/analysis/llm_analyzer.py, which prefers gemini-2.5-flash-lite at 1000 RPD free over gemini-2.5-flash at 250 RPD and rotates across all available keys on quota/availability errors): the first attempt annotated 12/24 docs before all three keys hit 429/503 on the larger first batch; a rotating retry recovered 10 more (22/24) via flash-lite; two of those had systematically weak regex-anchoring (flash-lite producing non-unique or malformed patterns that opf_annotate's own-document `finditer` count-!=-1 check silently drops), so a targeted fix pass re-ran just those plus the 2 fully-failed docs against gemini-2.5-flash first -- by then all three keys were fully quota-exhausted for flash, so those retries actually landed on the flash-lite fallback, recovering 2 more docs but leaving 2 irrecoverably thin (1 resolved span each) and 2 still at zero; those 2+2 were dropped, leaving 20 clean docs, split 14/3/3 (random, seed 20230916). Round F was initially the first batch in this corpus with NO subagent or human labeling step of any kind -- it passed mechanical validation cleanly (0 offset/overlap/label-space errors, 357 spans across 20 docs) but that only checks offsets/overlaps/label-space membership, not correctness. A quality-check request prompted a proper audit: 20 subagents (one per doc) independently judged every one of the 357 predicted spans against the annotation guideline and read each full document for missed anchors, finding only 61% span-level precision (217 correct / 357 predicted) plus 124 noted missed anchors -- see verification_note for the full breakdown. Rather than revert Round F (losing real signal and reopening G5) or leave it in gold unreviewed, a Round-E-style correction pass followed: 20 more subagents, each given the Gemini draft + that document's audit verdict as a starting point, produced final corrected labels (keep audit-confirmed spans, fix wrong_category/wrong_boundary, drop false_positive, add every missed anchor after re-verifying it, then an independent fresh read for anything still missed). This raised the total span count from 357 to 456 across the same 20 documents (same split assignment, same doc identities -- only the labels changed) and fixed the two most consequential defects: the systematic ref_normativa/fundamentacao_legal citation truncation (dropped leading art./artigo/Resolução tokens, ~40+ instances across the batch) and the repeated dispositivo_abertura/resultado misses (the single most operationally important category pair in the ontology, wrong or missing in a large fraction of Round F documents pre-correction). opf_annotate.py validate on the corrected 456-span set: 0 errors, 0 warnings (the one pre-correction warning, about acordao_decisorio/voto having zero support in this sentenca-only batch, is expected and resolved by the rest of the corpus already carrying those categories). The raw, uncorrected Gemini predictions were discarded after the correction subagents extracted what they needed from them -- only the corrected 456-span labels are in train/val/test.
